We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

We have guidance: steps forward: 1) carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse: Starting from target, we break amide bond to get carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So reverse: unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). Then sulfonamide formation forward: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. Reverse: sulfonamide -> amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we need three retrosynthetic steps: Step1: disconnection of amide (C=O-N) to give carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid) and aniline (the aniline attached to phenyl). Step2: disconnection of unsaturated acid to give aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl with aldehyde) and malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). Step3: disconnection of sulfonamide to give amine (the aniline) and sulfonyl chloride (the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl). However note that the sulfonamide is attached to first phenyl (para-methyl phenyl) with NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl which also has the unsaturated amide side chain. So the sulfonamide is between the first phenyl amine and sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So reverse: break S-N bond to give the aniline (first phenyl with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (i.e., 4-(... )-phenyl sulfonyl chloride). That sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the second phenyl with a chlorine on sulfonyl group.

Thus we need templates for amide formation (reverse: amide cleavage), for Doebner modification (reverse: unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid), and for sulfonamide formation (reverse: sulfonamide cleavage). We need to find template IDs for these transformations. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with appropriate functional groups broken/formed.

First, get list of functional groups.
